reviews.comment: The lectures were pretty decent and the course content was good, but the exams were very difficult for the amount of time we had and the final project was brutal.
The course covered a good amount of topics, and the lectures were decent, but the exams were very hard, and the final project was brutal.

Prof.Bobak conducts great lectures and is very knowledgeable. Take this class if you are interested in machine learning and not to get a CS elective out of the way. I felt the sample exams were not representative of the real exams both in terms of difficulty and length. Final project worth 25% of your grade that helps bring grade up at the end.

The prof is very absent. However, if you already have a solid background in machine learning, the class isn't too difficult to get through. That said, the professor is interesting to talk to about topics outside the course, especially when it comes to new research and ideas.

Clearly very passionate about machine learning and wants the students to succeed. The material is interesting, and Bobak does a good job at engaging the students. As for the exam, this is controversial, but I thought it was pretty fair. It looked just like the practice exam, but harder. The TA's discussions are not helpful.

Great Lectures! The prof clears every single doubt. The Homeworks are challenging but he gives out python notebooks which are really helpful and can help you understand a hard concept outside class during office hours. Two midterms, exams are conceptual based and a final project. Highly recommend 633 and the prof.

Though lecture is more conceptual orientated and no need to understand all of them to get works done, his lecture is one of the best lectures given in all undergraduate course I've taken in CSCE department. The exam requires understanding to the concept but not to an extreme extent. You're fine as long as you understand what you wrote on homework.

Lectures very conceptual-focused, which helps. Around 6-8 Homeworks, which have you create/train python models. He doesn't teach how to code, so you'll have to figure it out; do them early. Quizzes are fairly straightforward and purely conceptual based. 2 Exams, covers conceptual, debugging, and very basic math of ML models. 1 Semester Project (ok)

He cares a lot and gives many points for curves. However, his HWs can be confusing sometimes and the rubric for the HW is never given in advance so you don't know what is expected. Lectures can be full of fluff but his quizzes are pretty straightforward. Exams can be difficult but they are not cumulative.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Mortazavi is a very nice professor, he will give us a lot of extra credit on the exam, and the TA's OH is very useful, the exam review and review session will help a lot!

Hardest CS class I have ever taken. His lectures are 70 + pages long with extremely complicated math formulas that he expects you to understand without detailed explanation and use them in coding homeworks that he does not explain at all.

Mortazavi is overall a decent teacher. He cares about improving his courses and thinks through the way he teaches the class, which I appreciate. The HWs are very confusing and there are often hidden rubric points you have to meet or else you get points off. They are mostly all on the internet though. The tests are unpredictable, & reviews useless
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Is a decent lecturer but hws are very vague and quizzes are long and confusing. Hws also take a long time and he doesn't really explain them well. However, he is a pretty generous prof and will bump people and curve quizzes. Also, bonus points on homeworks are given if you don't turn anything in late. Definitely learned a lot of was frustrating.

the assignments he assigns are HARD. The materials are complicated enough, but also he does not explain well on the coding part. you maybe understand the math part, but you don't know how to put it in code because you don't know what functions to use or how the functions work. He expects you to auto learn all the codes that he did not provide.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read
